note: Three kinds of figure reach a surface here. Some are quoted from a claim and say so. Some are counted by compute.py from a fetched document, and the computation is named rather than the number being asserted. The six zeros on slide 7 are the third kind and the awkward one, because a count of what a document does NOT say cannot be quoted from it: compute.py counts them over the served bytes and RAISES rather than publishing if any is non-zero, so the frame cannot draw a zero the snapshot does not support.

aggregates.computed_by: compute.py N_KNOWLEDGE, the number of numbered knowledge statements its heading pattern finds in the attachment snapshot. It also corroborates: if a reported gap in the numbering is contradicted by the document printing that number anywhere, compute.py raises instead of handing the gap to a frame. That guard exists because the first build's pattern excluded a heading carrying a colon and published a missing chapter six that does not exist.

compute.py N_FOOTPRINT_TERMS, the machine-naming stems with at least one occurrence in the course text. The stem is what is counted, so algorithm covers algorithm-driven and algorithmic alike, which is why the frame prints the stem beside the count rather than either full word.

compute.py FOOTPRINT_POSITIONS, the word index of each of the five occurrences in the course text. Three of them fall between word 2675 and word 2689, which is inside c16's single clause, and the other two are 1331 and 1614. The frame draws each mark at its own measured position, so the claim is visible rather than asserted.
